findings.title: get_monitor_environment_context builds a display-friendly config but returns the raw model config
findings.body: In get_monitor_environment_context, the local variable `config` is computed as a copy of monitor.config with `schedule_type` replaced by its human-readable display value (`monitor.get_schedule_type_display()`), but the returned dict at line 168 uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of `config`. The local `config` is therefore dead code, and the monitor context emitted in the occurrence's event data always contains the raw numeric `schedule_type` rather than the display string. The transformation the function clearly intends to apply is silently never used. This was carried over from the old mark_failed.py code, but since it is being re-homed now is a good time to fix it: either return `config` in the dict or remove the dead computation.

findings.title: get_failure_reason docstring examples don't match the actual return values
findings.body: The docstring for get_failure_reason claims outputs like "3 missed check-ins detected" and "A failed check-in was detected", but the code actually produces "3 missed check-ins check-ins detected"-style strings (the format string is "%(problem_checkins)s check-ins detected", so the human status list is followed by a second "check-ins detected" suffix), and the singular case returns "An error check-in was detected" / "A missed check-in was detected" / "A timeout check-in was detected", never "A failed check-in was detected". The docstring also contains the typo "humam readible". Anyone using the docstring to understand the user-facing evidence text will be misled; update the examples (e.g. "3 missed check-ins check-ins detected" or better, restructure the sentence) to match reality.
